## Appeal Letter

|  |  |

| James W. Remillard  Director  Missouri State Emergency Management Agency  P.O. Box 116  Jefferson City, Missouri 65102 | Jarret Ficke  Public Works Director  City of Doniphan  110 N Grand Avenue  Doniphan, Missouri 63935 |

| Re: | Second Appeal – City of Doniphan, PA ID: 181-19792-00, FEMA-4872-DR-MO, Request for Public Assistance, Application Procedures |

Dear James W. Remillard and Jarret Ficke:

This is in response to the June 24, 2026 letter from the Missouri State Emergency Management Agency (Recipient), which forwarded the referenced second appeal on behalf of the City of Doniphan (City). The City is appealing the U.S. Department of Homeland Security’s Federal Emergency Management Agency’s (FEMA) denial of its Request for Public Assistance (RPA) and an associated $22,723.46 for debris removal, slope stabilization, and material costs.

As explained in the enclosed analysis, I have determined that the City did not submit the RPA within the RPA submission deadline and did not demonstrate extenuating circumstances beyond its or the Recipient’s control to justify extending the deadline. Accordingly, I am denying this appeal.

This determination is the final decision on this matter pursuant to 44 C.F.R. § 206.206.

                                                                          Sincerely,

                                                                               /S/

                                                                           Robert M. Pesapane

                                                                           Director, Public Assistance

Enclosure

cc:  Jay Van Der Werff

      Regional Administrator

      FEMA Region 7

## Appeal Analysis

**Background**

From March 30 to April 8, 2025, the state of Missouri was impacted by severe storms, straight-line winds, tornadoes, and flooding, resulting in a major disaster declared on May 21, 2025. The flooding damaged the City of Doniphan’s (City) park buildings, fences, and public works building; washed away and eroded roads; and clogged culverts. The deadline for eligible applicants to submit a Request for Public Assistance (RPA) was June 20, 2025.

On October 6, 2025, 108 days after the RPA submission deadline, the City submitted an RPA. The City requested FEMA accept and review its RPA, explaining its reasons for the late submission. The City asserted it believed it had submitted initial damage reports and documentation to the Missouri State Emergency Management Agency (Recipient) via email on April 25, 2025. However, it later discovered that the damage reports and documentation had not been delivered as intended on April 25, 2025 due to the size of the email and the attachments. The City also stated that, upon discovery of the undelivered documentation, it immediately reached out to the Recipient for assistance. On October 10, 2025, the Recipient submitted the RPA to FEMA.

On January 12, 2026, FEMA issued a Determination Memorandum (DM). FEMA found the City was ineligible for Public Assistance (PA) because it failed to submit the RPA before the June 20, 2025 submission deadline. FEMA explained that the City’s misunderstanding of the submission process and miscommunication with the Recipient were not extenuating circumstances beyond the control of either the City or the Recipient to justify an extension of the RPA submission deadline.

*First Appeal*

On February 11, 2026, the City submitted its first appeal, indicating it incurred an estimated $22,723.46 in labor and equipment costs for debris removal and slope stabilization and in material losses. Regarding the late RPA, the Applicant asserted there were extenuating circumstances beyond its control, specifically technical communication failures and clerical errors on the part of the Recipient and FEMA. The City reiterated that its April 25, 2025 attempt to submit its RPA by email to the Recipient was not received due to file size limitations within the Recipient’s email system. The City contended it was not a failure on its part, but a failure of the electronic medium used for transmission. The City also contended that FEMA erroneously filed the DM under different applicants which made it impossible for it to accurately monitor its submission status in a timely manner. On February 18, 2026, the Recipient transmitted the City’s first appeal to FEMA. The Recipient stated it did not support the appeal because the City did not provide evidence of extenuating circumstances beyond its control that resulted in the inability to submit an RPA within the required timeframe.

On May 12, 2026, the FEMA Region 7 Regional Administrator (RA) denied the appeal. FEMA found that the City submitted its RPA untimely, 108 days after the June 20, 2025 deadline. FEMA determined that the City’s cited technical communications issues did not constitute extenuating circumstances beyond the City’s or Recipient’s control to justify an extension of the RPA submission deadline. FEMA also noted that the City did not provide documentation of its attempt to email the Recipient before the deadline.

*Second Appeal*

The City submitted its second appeal of the denial of its late RPA request, reiterating its first appeal arguments. The City details its contacts with the Recipient from April 23 to 25, 2026, prior to submitting its initial claim and documentation, and its receipt of denial determinations involving other unrelated applicants and projects. It states that electric correspondence failures and possible clerical errors apparently played a part in its late RPA submission and FEMA’s denial. On June 24, 2026, the Recipient transmitted the City’s second appeal. The Recipient states it does not support the second appeal, reiterating the same reasons it provided with transmission of the City’s first appeal.

**Discussion**

If an applicant wishes to seek PA funding, it must first submit an RPA to FEMA via Grants Portal within 30 days after the respective area is designated. FEMA may extend this deadline if the recipient submits a written justification based on extenuating circumstances beyond the applicant’s or recipient’s control. Extenuating circumstances that may justify a time extension for RPA submittal include: (1) the applicant is only claiming categories of work that were not authorized for the respective area in the initial declaration; (2) delays were due to slow responses or other issues caused by FEMA; (3) FEMA’s Grants Portal was offline or otherwise unavailable on the date the applicant tried to submit the RPA and it was the same day as the deadline; and (4) communication systems were down for such an extended time period that applicants in the area were unable to receive or send information. The recipient is responsible for providing technical advice and assistance to all eligible applicants, ensuring all potential applicants are aware of available of PA, and submitting documents necessary for the award of grants.

Here, the disaster declaration date was May 21, 2025, making the 30-day RPA submission deadline June 20, 2025. The City submitted its RPA on October 6, 2025, which was 108 days after the established deadline. The City asserts that its RPA was late due to extenuating circumstances arising from technical communication failure. The City states it discovered the error in early October, almost six months after it claims it tried to send the email. The City also states it immediately contacted the Recipient to ask about FEMA assistance. However, there is no evidence in the administrative record showing the email to the Recipient, any delivery failure notice, or any communications from the City to the Recipient or FEMA about when the error was discovered. Additionally, the City does not provide any evidence of its inability to submit its RPA through Grants Portal, the transmittal means required under FEMA policy. Under FEMA policy, the City’s confusion, lack of knowledge regarding PA program submission requirements, and insufficient communication with the Recipient do not constitute extenuating circumstances beyond the control of either the City or the Recipient that justify a time extension of the RPA submittal deadline.

Lastly, the City’s appeal claims the original DM denying its late RPA was misfiled, and that the DM in its file referenced another applicant. The City argues these errors delayed its ability to track its submission. However, these errors occurred after the initial RPA deadline of June 20, 2025, and did not affect the City’s ability to timely submit its RPA. The City also received a corrected DM and was given time to appeal.

**Conclusion**

The City did not submit the RPA within the RPA submission deadline and did not demonstrate extenuating circumstances beyond its or the Recipient’s control to justify extending the deadline. Therefore, this appeal is denied.

   The Determination Memorandum (DM) was signed on October 31, 2025; however, a different applicant’s (Virgil Township) DM was uploaded to Grants Portal/Grants Manager in error. FEMA corrected the error by uploading the correct DM on January 12, 2026. The correct DM was also sent/received via certified mail on January 14, 2026.
2. [^](#ref-ftn2)

   Title 44 of the Code of Federal Regulations (C.F.R.) § 206.202(c) (2024); *Public Assistance Program and Policy Guide*, *Version 5* *Amended,*FP 104-009-2, at 45 (Jan. 6, 2025) [hereinafter *PAPPG*].

   44 C.F.R. § 206.202(b).
6. [^](#ref-ftn6)

   The Recipient does not support the City’s appeal. The Recipient also does not acknowledge any communication with the City before the City submitted its RPA in October 2025, nor does it claim that technical communication issues caused any delays in submitting the RPA.
7. [^](#ref-ftn7)

   *See* FEMA Second Appeal Analysis, *Faith Family* *Fellowship*, FEMA-4798-DR-TX, at 2 (Dec. 2, 2025) (finding short-term loss of electrical power following the disaster (where the Applicant was able to use other technology to search for information, communicate with the Recipient and FEMA) does not constitute extenuating circumstances beyond the Applicant’s or Recipient’s control); FEMA Second Appeal Analysis, *Congregation Shir Shalom of Westchester and Fairfield Counties,*FEMA-4500-DR-CT, at 3 (Mar. 12, 2024) (finding that the Applicant’s lack of knowledge and understanding of the PA program are not circumstances outside of the Applicant’s or Recipient’s control); FEMA Second Appeal Analysis, *Sierra County Fire Protection District #1*, FEMA-4558-CA, at 2-3

   (Nov. 24, 2021) (finding that confusion on the Applicant’s part and insufficient communication and coordination are not extenuating circumstances).
8. [^](#ref-ftn8)

   Similarly, the City’s submission and first appeal letter and each of the Recipient’s transmittal letters utilizing an incorrect PA ID (021-UIK73-00) also had no impact on the City’s ability to submit a timely RPA as the DM issued on October 31, 2025 provides the correct PA ID (181-19792-00).
